title: Video versus Direct Laryngoscopy for Tracheal Intubation of Critically Ill Adults
shortTitle: DEVICE: first-pass success with video laryngoscopy
summary: In 1,417 critically ill adults, video laryngoscopy achieved first-pass success in 85.1% versus 70.8% with direct laryngoscopy (difference 14.3 percentage points; 95% CI 9.9 to 18.7). Severe complications occurred in 21.4% versus 20.9% (difference 0.5 points; 95% CI -3.9 to 4.9).
whyItMatters: Video laryngoscopy improved first-pass success in ED and ICU intubations, largely performed by trainees; complication benefit was not demonstrated.
limitations: Stopped early for efficacy. Most operators were residents or fellows, limiting generalization to experienced operators.
population: Critically ill adults in 17 US EDs and ICUs.
primaryEndpoint: Successful intubation on the first attempt
evidenceNotes: Abstract reviewed; full-text access was not used.
